body: ## An oil-heated town of owners

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) shows Holden heating differently from the middle town. Fuel oil or kerosene warms 4,397 of 7,118 occupied homes (61.8%), the 9th-highest share of the 50 towns we serve and far above the middle town's 36.5%. Utility gas heats 1,450 (20.4%), which ranks 40th. Electricity heats 613 homes (8.6%, 36th), bottled gas 350 (4.9%, 22nd) and wood 155 (2.2%).

For an oil-heated home, a failed boiler or furnace raises a choice: another oil unit, a heat pump, or gas where a main runs on the street. An oil system also has a fuel tank, fuel deliveries and a chimney to think about.
## Owners, detached houses and almost no empty homes

Owners occupy 6,098 households (85.7%), and single-family detached houses make up 5,836 of the 7,177 housing units (81.3%), 19th highest of 50. Only 59 homes are vacant (0.8%), the 48th-highest vacancy rate against 3.6% for the middle town. Rental housing is just 14.3% of households. The median owner-occupied home is worth $409,800, 42nd of 50, against $579,150 for the middle town.
Holden ranks 29th of 50 for renter share, below the 16.4% of the middle town, and 33rd for homes in multi-unit buildings.
## Postwar growth and a newer crop of houses

The median Holden home was built in 1970. The biggest band is 1940 to 1959, with 1,807 homes (25.2%), which is a larger share than the 1960 to 1979 band (1,589 homes, 22.1%). Postwar houses often have modest insulation by today's standards, which is worth checking before a system is sized. Another 1,582 homes (22.0%) date from 2000 on, and 675 from 2010 on.
Pre-war housing is thin: 849 homes (11.8%) date from 1939 or earlier, 39th of 50. The remaining bands are spread fairly evenly across the later decades.

Between them sit 1,589 homes (22.1%) from 1960 to 1979 and 1,350 (18.8%) from 1980 to 1999. Equipment in houses of different ages can run from original systems to recent installs, so the first question at a visit is how old the system really is.
## Hills, rivers and a municipal light department

Holden was founded in 1741 on All Hallow's Eve, and its Town Square was donated by John Hancock, a former Governor of Massachusetts. The town covers 36.2 square miles, of which 35.0 is land. The landscape is hills and rivers, including the Quinapoxet, and the village of Jefferson is part of the town. Holden was named for Samuel Holden, a director of the Bank of England. It is bounded by Rutland on the west, Princeton on the northwest, Sterling and West Boylston on the east, Worcester on the southeast and Paxton on the southwest. Water covers 3.40% of the town's area.

Electricity comes from the Holden Municipal Light Department, a municipal utility. That changes the rebate picture: in towns served by municipal utilities, Mass Save heat pump rebates generally apply only if the home heats with natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor. Holden has few gas homes, so most households are likely to look to the municipal department's own heat pump program. See our [heat pump page](/cities/holden/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: How common is oil heat in Holden?
faq.a: Very common. Fuel oil or kerosene heats 61.8% of occupied Holden homes, 9th highest among the 50 towns we serve, while utility gas heats 20.4%. If you have oil, plan on a yearly cleaning and think about whether a gas hookup or heat pump fits your house.

faq.q: Does Mass Save pay for heat pumps in Holden?
faq.a: Usually not for oil homes. Holden is served by a municipal utility, and in those towns Mass Save heat pump rebates generally apply only to homes heated with natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor. Others follow the municipal program. Terms can change, so confirm both before buying.

faq.q: Is a gas main available on my Holden street?
faq.a: That depends on the street. Only 20.4% of homes use utility gas, so a main does not reach every street. Ask the gas company, or ask us at the estimate, because the answer decides whether conversion is realistic. A conversion also needs a permit pulled by a licensed plumber or gas fitter, plus a final inspection.

faq.q: Why does sizing matter for Holden houses?
faq.a: The old unit is not a reliable guide. Insulation and windows change over the years, and a system sized from the old unit may be too big for the house today. Holden's housing spans the 1940 to 1959 band (25.2%) and the 1960 to 1979 band (22.1%), so ages vary. We assess the home's heating load before we quote.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Oil heats 4,397 Holden homes and gas only 1,450, so a failed boiler or furnace usually raises one question first: another oil unit, a gas hookup or a heat pump. The tank, the chimney and the delivery routine are part of the decision.
body: ## An oil town's replacement decision

Holden ranks 9th of 50 towns for fuel oil and 40th for utility gas. Oil or kerosene heats 4,397 occupied homes (61.8%), gas heats 1,450 (20.4%), electricity 613 (8.6%), bottled gas 350 (4.9%) and wood 155 (2.2%). For most households a heating failure is an oil failure.
### Staying with oil

A new oil boiler or furnace is the like-for-like route, and it keeps the existing tank, chimney and piping in play. Check the tank and the chimney liner at the same time as the burner, since a new appliance is the moment to find a worn part. Sizing from the house, not from the old nameplate, avoids an oversized unit.
### Switching to gas

Only 20.4% of Holden homes use utility gas, so a main does not reach every street. Ask the gas company whether one passes your lot before you plan around a conversion. When one does, the work is for a licensed gas fitter and ends with an inspection, and the old oil tank has to be dealt with.
### Switching to a heat pump

A cold-climate heat pump can carry most of the year, with the oil boiler kept for the coldest days or retired. Holden has 613 electric-heat homes, a lower share than the middle town. Our [heat pump page](/cities/holden/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers the municipal-utility side of that choice.
### What the age of the housing tells us

The median Holden home was built in 1970, and the biggest group is 1,807 homes from 1940 to 1959. Equipment in houses of those ages may have been replaced already, so when you get a quote, ask whether the heating load was calculated, not guessed.
### Wood and other fuels
Wood heats 155 Holden homes and another 122 use other fuels or coal. If the main system fails, a stove alone may not keep a whole house warm for long, so plan the main system first.
### When it fails in winter
Call (508) 786-8755; we take emergency calls around the clock. To keep the next failure from happening at midnight, see the [maintenance page](/cities/holden/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: Is oil still the main heating fuel in Holden?
faq.a: Yes. Oil or kerosene heats 61.8% of occupied Holden homes, which is the 9th-highest share of the 50 towns we serve. Utility gas heats only 20.4%. That makes oil replacement the town's most common heating decision, with gas and heat pumps as the main alternatives to compare against it.

faq.q: Should a Holden homeowner replace an oil boiler with a new oil boiler?
faq.a: It is a reasonable choice if you have no gas main and no plan for a heat pump. Modern oil equipment is more efficient than an old unit, and you keep the tank and chimney. Compare it in writing with the heat pump option, because the long-term fuel cost differs by house.

faq.q: What should I check on an old Holden oil boiler before it fails?
faq.a: Look for rust around the base, water on the floor, soot near the burner and a tank that is old or leaning. Note the age, since replacement becomes likelier with age. About 59.1% of Holden homes were built before 1980, so many boilers there are working beyond their first install.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Holden has 5,836 detached houses, 422 townhouses and 888 units in multi-unit buildings, and mostly oil heat. That mix means many houses have no ducts, so ductless cooling is often the practical route.
body: ## Cooling houses that were built for heat

Of Holden's 7,177 housing units, 5,836 are single-family detached (81.3%) and 422 are attached townhouses (5.9%). Two-unit buildings hold 56, buildings with 3 to 4 units hold 90 and buildings with five or more hold 742. Together, multi-unit buildings account for 888 units (12.4%).
### Oil-heated houses

An oil home may have a boiler with baseboards or radiators, which means no ducts, or a furnace with ducts. Many older houses were built without central air. Ductless mini-splits are the usual answer, with an indoor head in each zone and a small outdoor unit.
### Houses with a furnace

Where a forced-air furnace already moves air through ducts, a central air conditioner can sometimes share them. The ducts have to be right-sized, sealed and reachable. In the 1,450 gas homes and others with forced air, that is the first thing to check.
### Ranch and postwar houses

The largest age band in Holden is 1940 to 1959, with 1,807 homes. In a postwar house, attic insulation and venting can matter as much as the air conditioner. Sizing should reflect the actual envelope.
### Hills and placement

Holden's landscape is hills and rivers, and the town covers 35.0 square miles of land. On a sloped lot the outdoor unit needs level footing and drainage away from the foundation. Keep it clear of leaves, snow drifts and downspouts.
### Heat pump option

A heat pump cools in summer and heats in winter, which for an oil household can turn a cooling purchase into a partial heating replacement. See the [heat pump page](/cities/holden/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits). Whether it makes sense depends on the load of the house.
### Repair or replace
A unit that cools poorly may need a cleaning or a part. Replacement is more likely when the compressor fails on aging equipment. We write both options down so you can compare.

faq.q: Can I add air conditioning to a Holden house with a boiler?
faq.a: Yes. Because a boiler house has no ducts, a ductless mini-split is the usual choice. Each indoor head cools one zone and connects to an outdoor unit through a small line. A technician can say how many heads your layout needs and where the outdoor unit can go.

faq.q: Is central air possible in an older Holden house?
faq.a: Sometimes. If there is a forced-air furnace with ducts in good condition, central air may share them. In houses built from 1940 to 1959, the largest age group in town at 1,807 homes, ducts may be absent or undersized. A technician checks before recommending central air or ductless.

faq.q: Should I size a Holden air conditioner by the old unit?
faq.a: No. Insulation, windows and shade change over the years, so the old unit may be too big or too small. An oversized unit cools quickly, shuts off early and leaves the air clammy. A load calculation based on the house as it is today avoids both problems.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Holden's electricity comes from a municipal light department, and 4,397 of its homes heat with oil. The rebate path usually follows the municipal program, and the choice for most households is oil versus heat pump.
body: ## Heat pumps in an oil-heated, municipal-electric town

Holden Municipal Light Department serves the town, so Mass Save's whole-home rebate generally reaches only homes heated with sponsor-supplied natural gas, while others use the department's own program. We do not quote what that program pays; ask the department. The Mass Save rules are on our [heat pump overview](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### The oil households

With 4,397 homes on oil, Holden has a large pool of households that could trade a delivered fuel for electricity. Oil ranks 9th of 50. A cold-climate heat pump can carry most of the year, with the boiler kept as backup for the coldest days. Bottled gas serves another 350 homes, and wood 155.
### The few gas homes

Only 1,450 homes use utility gas, ranking 40th. Those homes are the ones that might fall under the Mass Save gas-sponsor rule. If you have gas, confirm with the sponsor before assuming either program applies.
### Electric homes

Electricity heats 613 Holden homes (8.6%). If that heat is baseboard or an electric furnace, a heat pump can deliver the same warmth with less electricity, and the municipal department's program is the place to ask about help.
### The age test for weatherization

Mass Save's whole-home rule asks the house to count as weatherized. In Holden, 1,582 homes (22.0%) date from 2000 or later, a group that meets the age test directly. The other 1,350 homes from 1980 to 1999 and the 4,245 built before 1980 need an assessment first. The largest older group is 1,807 homes from 1940 to 1959.
### Ducted or ductless

A house with working ducts can take a ducted system. Boiler houses with baseboards or radiators have no ducts, so ductless heads fit better: one per zone. Detached houses are 81.3% of the stock, so ductless heads in a detached house are the typical design.
### Sizing comes first
We assess the home's heating load before quoting a system. For cooling-only work, see the [air conditioning page](/cities/holden/air-conditioning-installation-repair).

faq.q: Does Mass Save pay for a heat pump in an oil-heated Holden home?
faq.a: Generally not. Holden has a municipal electric utility, and in such towns the Mass Save heat pump rebate generally applies only to homes heated with natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor. Oil homes look to the municipal department's own program. Confirm with the department and masssave.com before you buy.

faq.q: Can a Holden oil home keep its boiler and add a heat pump?
faq.a: Yes. In a partial-home setup, the heat pump handles most of the year and the boiler covers the coldest stretch. With 61.8% of homes on oil, this is the most common version of the question in town. You keep the tank and yearly cleaning, but you cut the amount of oil you buy.

faq.q: What do I need to find out before choosing a heat pump in Holden?
faq.a: Which program applies to your home, whether the house meets the weatherization test, and what the heating load is. Our heating-load assessment answers the last one. The first two come from the municipal department and masssave.com. Having those answers before quotes arrive makes it easier to compare them fairly.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Holden has 6,098 owner households and 1,020 renter households, and oil heats most homes. The yearly oil cleaning is the town's core maintenance visit, with gas, electric and bottled-gas checks following their own routines.
body: ## Maintenance in a town of owners
Owners occupy 6,098 Holden households (85.7%) and renters occupy 1,020 (14.3%). With 4,397 homes on oil, the yearly cleaning is the main appointment of the heating season.
### The oil visit

The burner and boiler or furnace are cleaned, the nozzle and filter are replaced and combustion is tested. The technician looks over the tank, the fuel line and the chimney connection. Booking in late summer leaves time to order a part before cold weather arrives.
### Why oil needs it every year
Soot builds up on heat-transfer surfaces and a worn nozzle changes the flame. Neither is visible from the living room. A skipped year often means the first sign is a no-heat call in January.
### Gas, 1,450 homes
A gas check covers the burner, heat exchanger, venting and controls, with carbon monoxide testing.
### Electric and heat pump homes, 613 homes
Filters, coils and the outdoor unit need attention, and a mini-split has one filter per indoor head. A heat pump added next to an oil boiler means two systems to maintain.
### Bottled gas, 350 homes
The same checks as natural gas, with a look at the tank and regulator.
### Rentals
With 1,020 renter households, rentals are a small part of the town. A landlord owning one or two units can schedule a single visit for all the equipment before the season starts.
### Houses from different decades

Holden's housing is spread over many decades: 849 homes from 1939 or earlier, 1,807 from 1940 to 1959, 1,589 from 1960 to 1979, 1,350 from 1980 to 1999 and 1,582 from 2000 on. Equipment in those groups ranges from long-serving boilers to recent installs, so the first question at a visit is how old the system really is.
### Prepare for the visit
Have the fuel type, equipment age, make and model and any symptom ready. If the unit looks worn out, see the [heating page](/cities/holden/heating-installation-repair).

faq.q: How often should a Holden oil boiler be cleaned?
faq.a: Every year, before the heating season. With 61.8% of homes on oil, it is the town's most common service. The visit removes soot, replaces the nozzle and filter, tests combustion and checks the tank and chimney connection. Late summer works well because parts can be ordered before it turns cold.

faq.q: Can I skip maintenance in a newer Holden house?
faq.a: Not really. Newer equipment still needs filters changed, combustion or refrigerant checked and the outdoor unit kept clear. Holden has 1,582 homes built since 2000, and efficiency drops in any system when parts get dirty. A yearly visit lowers the chance of a breakdown.

faq.q: What can I do between professional visits?
faq.a: Change filters on schedule, keep clear space around the boiler or furnace, and keep outdoor units free of leaves and snow. Check that the tank has fuel and the thermostat has fresh batteries. These steps do not replace a visit, but they remove several simple causes of a no-heat call.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Holden has 849 homes from 1939 or earlier, 1,807 from 1940 to 1959 and 1,582 from 2000 on, with almost no vacancy. Air quality questions differ by age band, and by whether a house burns oil, gas or wood.
body: ## Air quality in houses of different ages

The ACS 2022 splits Holden's 7,177 housing units into 849 homes from 1939 or earlier (11.8%), 1,807 from 1940 to 1959 (25.2%), 1,589 from 1960 to 1979 (22.1%), 1,350 from 1980 to 1999 (18.8%) and 1,582 from 2000 on (22.0%). Of the newest group, 675 date from 2010 on.
### Older and postwar houses

Houses built before 1980 are often leaky enough to exchange air on their own. That lets some indoor pollutants out and lets outdoor dust and pollen in. Holden has 4,245 such homes. Before heavy renovation of old materials, ask a qualified specialist about testing.
### Newer, tighter houses

Holden ranks 19th of 50 for homes built since 2010. A recent house is usually tight, so cooking fumes, moisture and furnishing chemicals stay indoors unless fans and ventilation move them out. Bath fans and a range hood vented outdoors help most.
### Combustion and indoor air

With 4,397 oil homes, 1,450 gas homes, 350 bottled-gas homes and 155 wood-heated homes, combustion equipment is the norm. Carbon monoxide detectors and annual equipment checks matter more than any air cleaner. A wood stove adds smoke and ash to the list of things to manage.
### Basements, hills and rivers

Holden has hills and rivers, and the town is 3.40% water. A damp basement has a source: groundwater, a pipe or warm summer air on cool masonry. Fix the source first, then use a dehumidifier to manage the air.
### Tightly occupied housing
The vacancy rate is 0.8%, so very few homes sit empty. Occupied homes produce moisture and fumes every day from cooking, bathing and heating. Ventilation that runs matters more than a seasonal fix.
### Ducts and filters
Duct cleaning is for ducts with visible mold, heavy dirt or renovation debris. Otherwise start with the filter. See the [maintenance page](/cities/holden/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: Do I need to clean the ducts in my Holden house?
faq.a: Only in specific cases: visible mold, heavy dirt or renovation debris. For most homes, a better filter changed on schedule comes first. A house with a boiler and radiators has no ducts, in which case there is nothing to clean. We inspect and say what we would do.

faq.q: How can I reduce moisture in a Holden basement?
faq.a: Find the source first. It may be groundwater, a leaking pipe or humid air meeting cool masonry. A dehumidifier then manages the air in the space. If you have an oil boiler or furnace in the basement, keep the area dry, since damp conditions can shorten the life of the equipment.

faq.q: Does a wood stove or oil boiler affect my indoor air?
faq.a: Combustion appliances can add carbon monoxide, smoke or fumes if venting is poor. Holden has 155 wood-heated and 4,397 oil-heated homes. Have the venting inspected yearly, use working carbon monoxide detectors and keep the chimney clear. An air cleaner does not replace correct venting.
